query: "Large-scale empirical study on developer engagement and expertise in configurable software systems analyzing variability via preprocessor directives, assessing workload distribution across developers, evaluating effectiveness of expertise metrics using mining repositories of 25 CSS projects, focusing on software product lines and variable code expertise identification."

response.query: Large-scale empirical study on developer engagement and expertise in configurable software systems analyzing variability via preprocessor directives, assessing workload distribution across developers, evaluating effectiveness of expertise metrics using mining repositories of 25 CSS projects, focusing on software product lines and variable code expertise identification.
response.answer: A large-scale study analyzed developer engagement and expertise in configurable software systems, focusing on workload distribution and expertise metrics across 25 projects. The study used preprocessor directives to analyze variability and identified variable code expertise. Results showed significant insights into developer workload and expertise.

results.title: M. Acher, Full Professor, PhD (personal webpage)
results.content: # Mathieu Acher, Full Professor, PhD. ### Personal webpage of Mathieu Acher, Full Professor, PhD. I am junior research fellow at Institut Universitaire de France (IUF) since september 2021, and a member of the DiverSE team (Inria/IRISA/CNRS) since september 2012. I was Associate Professor (tenured) at Université of Rennes 1 and ISTIC from 2012 to 2022. I am interested in any form of *variability* (in software, in computational science, in artificial intelligence, in videos, in 3D printing, in data, etc.). Software product lines, configurable systems, generators, configurations/configurators, product comparison matrix, customizations, feature models, or domain-specific languages are some keywords of my research and teaching. For more details, see below my research interests, software development, publications, PhD thesis, or even HDR manuscript! **"Handbook of Re-Engineering Software Intensive Systems into Software Product Lines" is finally out and available on Springer 20 chapters and 78 contributors from academia and industries about reverse engineering variability (feature location, feature model synthesis), re-engineering product lines and configurable systems, with many methods, automated techniques, frameworks, tools, and case studies.**.
